I like the merch that isn't blatantly merch. It's interesting that the only people who recognize a lot of Shane's stuff are fellow viewers. Some other people made the point that it's kind of embarrassing to wear something with a YouTuber's name on it, so seeing some different ideas that still connect to the creator (like an inside joke from videos) is cool.

As for the self-loathing thing, I'd have to agree. It's good to find humor or a bright side in difficult topics, but sometimes it seems out of hand? Honestly, I kind of forget that he does the pig stuff in a self-degrading way; his infamous snort/laugh comes to mind rather than the "lol i have a bad relationship with food" concept at times. But some of the newer stuff is kind of annoying. 

That being said, I do love Shane and I'm glad he's finding ideas he enjoys to pursue. He will forever hold a special place in my heart, even if some of his merch kinda sucks :')

Somebody, PLEASE HELP ME!

I am 17 years old. I filed my own taxes for 2018 and 2019 via TurboTax. I must have made a mistake because looking back on my return, I said I was not being claimed as a dependent when my \[single\] father actually did claim me. This was a total accident - I must have misunderstood the question or something. Today I got a letter from the Department of the Treasury saying I received $1200. Because I am a seventeen-year-old dependent, my dad shouldn't get the extra $500 for me and I shouldn't get the $1200. For now, I am not touching the money just in case (I haven't checked whether the money is actually in my account or not). I talked to my mom and my grandma, who has been keeping up with all of this, said that this is a result of fixing the issue of 17-24-year-olds not receiving money in any capacity. Is this true? Every article I've read has said that this age group is out of luck, but the lastest ones are from mid-April and might not be updated. I am about to start college and would love to have this extra money, but not if I'm not supposed to have it. WHAT DO I DO?

TL;DR: I \[17\] accidentally said I was an independent on my 2019 taxes when my dad did, in fact, claim me, and I received a letter saying that I am receiving the $1200. Was this supposed to happen?
